items.title: A build utility can poison Linux
items.oneliner: Researchers showed one compromised GNU strip can backdoor nearly every NixOS binary. Supply chain trust just moved downstack.

items.title: Nix packages now run in browsers
items.oneliner: Trunix runs 310,083 Nix package versions in-browser via WebAssembly. Reproducible demos just got dramatically easier to share.

items.title: Asahi Linux reaches Apple M3 Macs
items.oneliner: Asahi now officially supports M3 Macs, but GPU acceleration, sleep, and HDMI still lag. Porting Apple silicon remains brutal.

items.title: IBM pushes quantum throughput sharply higher
items.oneliner: IBM says Nighthawk r2 runs over 100,000 circuits per second, 25x Heron. Speed is becoming a first-class metric.

items.title: Chrome again spares Google site data
items.oneliner: Chrome again preserved Google.com data despite auto-delete settings. Privacy bugs look different when the browser owner benefits.

items.title: DNS abuse is now industrial scale
items.oneliner: About 8.5 million new gTLDs were blacklisted in 2025 alone. Domain registration has become scam infrastructure.

items.title: Australia is deepening state surveillance
items.oneliner: Australia is expanding Palantir and Cellebrite-style surveillance. Data tooling is becoming public-sector power, not just enterprise software.

items.title: AI is breaking code review workflows
items.oneliner: Martin Fowler's site argues AI code volume is overwhelming review queues. Teams need earlier feedback, not bigger PR backlogs.

items.title: Debian Code Search drops its cgo dependency
items.oneliner: Debian Code Search replaced its last cgo path with Go SIMD and AVX512. Performance work is getting more portable.

items.title: Europe gets a real commercial launcher
items.oneliner: Isar Aerospace reached orbit and deployed payloads on its second flight. European launch independence just became more credible.
